question.problem:
The probability distribution of the random variable $X$ is given below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=2,$ calculate $\text{Var}[\sqrt{3}X].$ 

| $x$ | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ |
question.worked_solution:
Recall that for any random variable $X$ and constant $a,$ we have

$$
\text{Var}[aX]={a}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X].
$$

In our case, $a=\sqrt{3}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[\sqrt{3}X] & ={\sqrt{3}}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =3\cdot \text{Var}[X].\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the variance of $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

Additionally, we're given that $\text{E}[X]=2.$ 

We start by computing $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={0}^{2}\cdot f(0)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{4}^{2}\cdot f(4) \\  & =4\cdot \frac{1}{3}+16\cdot \frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{20}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{20}{3}-{2}^{2} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[\sqrt{3}X] & =3\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =3\cdot \frac{8}{3} \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$
